text.tspan: Containers on AWS: ECS, EKS, Fargate, ECR, and the ECS launch types
EC2 launch type: YOU provision + maintain the EC2 instances
• Launch Docker containers on AWS = launch ECS TASKS on ECS CLUSTERS
• Each EC2 instance runs the ECS agent to register in the cluster
• AWS takes care of starting / stopping containers
• You patch, scale and pay for the instances
Fargate launch type: NO EC2 instances to manage
each task gets its own ENI (awsvpc) and isolation boundary
• It's all serverless: you just create TASK DEFINITIONS
• AWS runs tasks for the CPU / RAM you ask for
• To scale: just increase the number of tasks
Newer than the course slides' text (docs, 2025-2026)
• ECS Managed Instances: EC2 instances that AWS provisions, patches and scales for you ("Fargate simplicity, EC2 flexibility":
choose instance types, GPUs). Listed by the docs as a launch type AND a capacity provider type.
• EXTERNAL launch type = ECS Anywhere (your own servers / VMs).
• Capacity providers (Fargate, Fargate Spot, Auto Scaling group, Managed Instances) are the recommended way to launch tasks.
• ECS Express Mode: one image → a Fargate web service with load balancer (AWS App Runner is closed to new customers).
• "Don't want to manage servers / serverless containers" → Fargate. "Need control of the instance (GPU, custom AMI, daemon)" → EC2 launch type.
• ECS = AWS API; EKS = Kubernetes API. Both can run on EC2 or Fargate. ECR is the registry for both.
